what: Every problem in the SAIR Lean Kernel Challenge, measured the same way: can the Lean kernel reduce the shipped reference starter at the judged sizes, and what does a replacement cost. Times are seconds of wall clock in one GitHub Actions job per problem, starter and candidate in the same job on the same runner, at upstream commit 940f0a2ead23ef70ab1387edabb347e629111edd.
caveat: Wall time on a shared runner varies by about twenty per cent between runs; the same sha256 starter measured 47.89 and 59.60 seconds on two runs of the same code. Comparisons are therefore only made within a single job. The competition's own metric is a hardware instruction count read through perf_event_open, which a virtualised runner does not expose, so none of these numbers is an official score.
reduces_key: whether the kernel could reduce impl n to the specification's own value at the judged sizes at all

problems.name: partition
problems.method: whole dynamic-programming row packed into one Nat
problems.note: totals over the six judged sizes, not a single case

problems.name: ca-rule110
problems.method: whole 256-cell automaton row packed into one Nat
problems.note: operation counts under the paper's own step model, not wall time

problems.name: fib
problems.method: none: the starter is Mathlib's fast doubling and was left alone
problems.note: 1.78 s of that is process startup, so the kernel work at n = 150000 is about 0.36 s

problems.name: polydisc
problems.method: none: measured competitive and left alone

problems.name: permanent
problems.method: sparse rows: the non-zero cells extracted once instead of scanned per node
problems.note: 3.1x at the hardest judged dimension; the proof rests on propext alone

problems.name: sha256
problems.method: message schedule fused into the rounds, so no list is built per block
problems.note: about eleven per cent, far less than removing roughly 65,000 allocations suggested; the cost is the round function, not the plumbing

problems.name: primecount
problems.defect: Nat.minFac dispatches through minFacAux, which is well-founded recursion
problems.method: trial division with an explicit fuel, bounded by d*d <= p rather than by Nat.sqrt
problems.note: the intermediate figure is an unbounded downward walk, kept as SubmissionLinear.lean

problems.name: mertens
problems.defect: ArithmeticFunction.moebius reaches Nat.minFac through Squarefree and the prime factorisation
problems.method: structural minFac proved equal to Nat.minFac, then Mathlib's own characterisation of moebius
